<description>
In a JSON-RPC batch, an element that is not an object gets an error reply with the id and version of the element before it.

`ExecuteHTTPRPC` parses every element of a batch into the same request object, and `parse()` throws on a non-object before it sets `id` and `m_json_version`. For `[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"getblockcount","id":"X"}, 2]` the reply has two objects with `"id":"X"`, one with a result and one with an error. If the first element is a notification, the error is dropped. I give each element its own copy of the request, which holds only the HTTP fields, so the error is the one the first element of a batch already gets. The new case in `interface_rpc.py` fails on master and passes with this change.
</description>

<commits>
5861dd29a7 rpc: parse each batch element into its own request

In a JSON-RPC batch, an element that is not an object gets an error
reply with the id and version of the element before it. A client that
matches replies by id can take that error for the result of the
previous call. If the previous element was a 2.0 notification, the
error is dropped.

Every element was parsed into the same JSONRPCRequest. I give each
element its own copy of the request before parsing, which holds only
the HTTP fields at that point. The functional test covers the two
cases.
</commits>

diff --git a/src/httprpc.cpp b/src/httprpc.cpp
index 0981de5f97..ad930f13ed 100644
--- a/src/httprpc.cpp
+++ b/src/httprpc.cpp
@@ -157,15 +157,19 @@ UniValue ExecuteHTTPRPC(const UniValue& valRequest, JSONRPCRequest& jreq, HTTPSt
                 // Batches never throw HTTP errors, they are always just included
                 // in "HTTP OK" responses. Notifications never get any response.
                 UniValue response;
+                // Each element gets its own copy of the unparsed request, so
+                // that nothing parsed from one element ends up in the reply to
+                // the next
+                JSONRPCRequest elem_jreq{jreq};
                 try {
-                    jreq.parse(valRequest[i]);
-                    response = JSONRPCExec(jreq, /*catch_errors=*/true);
+                    elem_jreq.parse(valRequest[i]);
+                    response = JSONRPCExec(elem_jreq, /*catch_errors=*/true);
                 } catch (UniValue& e) {
-                    response = JSONRPCReplyObj(NullUniValue, std::move(e), jreq.id, jreq.m_json_version);
+                    response = JSONRPCReplyObj(NullUniValue, std::move(e), elem_jreq.id, elem_jreq.m_json_version);
                 } catch (const std::exception& e) {
-                    response = JSONRPCReplyObj(NullUniValue, JSONRPCError(RPC_PARSE_ERROR, e.what()), jreq.id, jreq.m_json_version);
+                    response = JSONRPCReplyObj(NullUniValue, JSONRPCError(RPC_PARSE_ERROR, e.what()), elem_jreq.id, elem_jreq.m_json_version);
                 }
-                if (!jreq.IsNotification()) {
+                if (!elem_jreq.IsNotification()) {
                     reply.push_back(std::move(response));
                 }
             }
